I read this as **out**. The words are on the page, but LeCun did not hold a qualifying role in August 2015.

**The page.** The page opened. It is Tom Simonite's MIT Technology Review feature "Teaching Machines to Understand Us", dated 6 August 2015. The candidate sentence appears word for word: "LeCun guesses that virtual helpers with a mastery of language unprecedented for software will be available in just two to five years." This is the reporter's paraphrase, not a quote from LeCun. The article's quotation marks only begin with the next sentences ("There is the same phenomenon that we were observing just before 2012…"). So it is a news report, which would make it "coverage only" at best.

**Part 1, the role: fails.** The article says Facebook hired him in December 2013 and "put him in charge of a new artificial–intelligence research group, FAIR". In 2015 he led a research lab inside Facebook. That is not chief executive, founder-leader or chair of a company. It is also not the company's named chief scientist, a title his role history dates from about 2018. The rule reads that narrowly, so this is out. A reviewer might decide that heading FAIR was effectively speaking for Facebook as its top AI scientist, and that is the point to check. Even then, the most this could be is "pass, coverage only".

**The other three parts would pass:**
- **Part 2:** it is forward-looking and about AI: language-capable virtual assistants becoming available.
- **Part 3:** it gives a span, "two to five years" from August 2015. Taking the later end gives a due date of 2020.
- **Part 4:** the only source is this report, so it could be entered only as coverage, with no quote.
